sources.title: Conjunctivitis in Dogs — Overview
sources.chunk: Canine conjunctivitis presents with conjunctival hyperemia, discharge (serous, mucoid, or purulent), and blepharospasm. Differential includes KCS, corneal ulcer, uveitis, and glaucoma. Fluorescein stain and Schirmer tear test are core diagnostics.

sources.title: Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca (Dry Eye)
sources.chunk: KCS causes reduced tear production with mucoid discharge, corneal drying, and potential ulceration. Schirmer tear test confirms diagnosis. Chronic cases may show corneal vascularization or pigmentation.

sources.title: Corneal Ulcers and Abrasions
sources.chunk: Corneal ulcers cause pain, blepharospasm, and fluorescein uptake. Cannot be ruled out by photo alone. Deep or infected ulcers require prompt veterinary care.

sources.title: Allergic Skin Disease — Client Education Concepts
sources.chunk: Canine allergic dermatitis often presents with pruritus, erythema, and recurrent secondary pyoderma. Flea, food, and environmental allergens are common triggers. Cytology helps distinguish infection from primary allergy.

sources.title: Bacterial Pyoderma in Dogs
sources.chunk: Superficial pyoderma shows papules, pustules, and epidermal collarettes. Deep pyoderma may present with nodules and draining tracts. Cytology and culture guide antibiotic choice.

sources.title: Demodicosis in Dogs
sources.chunk: Demodicosis causes patchy to diffuse alopecia, often without significant pruritus initially. Skin scrape confirms mites. Juvenile-onset forms differ from adult immunosuppression-associated disease.

sources.title: Dermatophytosis (Ringworm)
sources.chunk: Dermatophytosis causes circular alopecia with scaling; some lesions are pruritic. Wood's lamp is insensitive in dogs; fungal culture is preferred for confirmation.

sources.title: Periodontal Disease Staging Concepts
sources.chunk: Periodontal disease progresses from gingivitis to attachment loss. Visual tartar grade correlates loosely with need for professional cleaning. Full assessment requires probing and dental radiographs under anesthesia.

sources.title: Periodontal Disease in Dogs
sources.chunk: Periodontal disease includes plaque, calculus, gingivitis, and periodontitis. Oral pain may reduce appetite. Fractured teeth with pulp exposure require extraction or endodontic therapy.

sources.title: Freedom Paws Urgent Assessment Policy
sources.source: Freedom Paws internal — severe conditions DB
sources.chunk: ViT Pro uses conservative urgency escalation: when severe-condition congruency meets threshold, recommend prompt veterinary evaluation. Never state that a serious condition is ruled out based on photo alone.

sources.title: Basic Ophthalmic Diagnostics
sources.chunk: Core ophthalmic diagnostics include menace response, dazzle reflex, fluorescein stain, Schirmer tear test, and tonometry when glaucoma is suspected.

sources.title: ViT Pro CDS Language Standard
sources.source: Freedom Paws ViT Pro Phase V0
sources.chunk: Reports use decision-support language: findings suggest consideration of listed differentials. Confidence bands (low/medium/high) reflect photo-limited certainty. Definitive diagnosis requires in-clinic examination and appropriate diagnostics.
